title: Forty subjects
hook: a newcomer is handed one verse as a test; his answer becomes a book with forty ways to meditate
tomorrow: how you sweep a floor might show which one suits you. how?

segments.voice: Last week the guide closed: a guide for living, meant for an ordinary Tuesday, ending with a bow to the good friend. A new book opens today, and it starts with a test.
screen: `A GUIDE FOR LIVING.` → `A NEW BOOK, AND A TEST.`

segments.voice: Some job interviews skip the résumé and slide one problem across the table: solve this. Tradition says that's how Buddhaghosa was welcomed at the Great Monastery in Sri Lanka. The senior monks gave the newcomer a single verse. It asks: there's a tangle inside and a tangle outside, and people are caught in it; who can untangle this tangle? His answer grew into a whole book, the Visuddhimagga, the Path of Purification. And the story adds a twist. The gods hid his manuscript, and he wrote it again. They hid it a second time, and he wrote it a third. When all three copies were laid side by side, they matched word for word.
screen: `ONE PROBLEM. SOLVE THIS.` → `WHO CAN UNTANGLE THIS TANGLE?` → `THREE COPIES, WORD FOR WORD.`

segments.voice: Deep inside that book is a list, and it answers last week's question: which way in is yours? The word is kammatthana, a meditation subject, the thing you work with when you sit. Buddhaghosa lists forty. Ten kasinas: discs of earth, water, fire, wind, colors and light to gaze at. Ten kinds of foulness, the body after death. Ten recollections: the Buddha, the teaching, the community, generosity, death, the breath, and more. Four divine abodes: loving-kindness, compassion, gladness, and equanimity. Four formless states. One perception, of food. One defining, of the elements of the body. Forty. And here's the surprise: this isn't a menu where every dish suits everyone. Some subjects fit some people and not others, and Buddhaghosa spends pages on how to match them. Only a couple he calls useful for everyone, like loving-kindness and remembering death. So the answer to which one is yours is: the one that fits you. Same house, forty doors. A door that's wrong for you may be exactly right for the person beside you.
screen: `KAMMATTHANA: WHAT YOU WORK WITH.` · `DISCS, FOULNESS, RECOLLECTIONS…` · `NOT EVERY DOOR SUITS EVERYONE.` · `A COUPLE SUIT ALL.` · then, large: `FORTY DOORS.`

segments.voice: Read the list slowly as it comes up on the screen, one group at a time: discs, foulness, recollections, divine abodes, formless states, food, elements. Don't choose anything. Just notice which door you lean toward and which you lean away from, and let both be information.
screen: `10 KASINAS · 10 FOULNESS · 10 RECOLLECTIONS` → `4 DIVINE ABODES · 4 FORMLESS STATES` → `1 PERCEPTION · 1 DEFINING`

segments.voice: Kammatthana: a meditation subject, the thing you work with in meditation. Buddhaghosa lists forty of them.
Carry this: forty doors, one house, and no door wrong for everyone. That's day one of forty.

screen: `DAY 1506 COUNTS.` → `THE FORTY SUBJECTS · 1 OF 40.` → `TOMORROW: HOW YOU SWEEP A FLOOR. WHAT DOES IT SHOW?`

howItsDone: In Theravada practice the Visuddhimagga is studied as a guide to meditation; a teacher may give a student one subject, such as the breath or loving-kindness, and add others over time.
